name: RobStride 00
_comment_source: Electrical/mechanical figures from the published RobStride 00 datasheet table. Phase resistance, inductance and all thermal parameters are NOT published and are estimated by the tool - see the ASSUMED PARAMETERS section of any report.

datasheet.title: RobStride RS00 User Manual
datasheet._note: revision is the vendor's filename stamp; version/date are from the manual's own section 7 Version History. The vendor's version field is inert: the 260713 revision STILL declares v1.0 dated 2025-11-25, seven months and several real spec changes after the 251210 revision did. The sha256 is the only reliable identity - verify with 'eval_actuator.py --check-datasheets'.

gear_eff.note: back-solved from vendor Kt_out=1.48 Nm/Arms against Ke=9.5 Vrms/kRPM

Ke_Vrms_per_kRPM.note: datasheet back-EMF, line-to-line RMS per 1000 rotor rpm

kt_sat_derate.note: 14 Nm actual peak vs 16.2 Nm linear extrapolation of Kt

tau_cont_out_spec.note: vendor 'rated load'; ambient and mounting unspecified

T_winding_max.note: manual 1.3.13 states the overload test constrains the winding to 145 degC (actual insulation limit 180 degC). This is the vendor's own design constraint and supersedes the previous Class-B-minus-margin estimate of 120 degC.

notes: Vendor rated torque of 5 N.m is quoted with no stated ambient temperature or mounting condition, so it cannot be taken as a continuous rating in an enclosed robot arm. This tool computes the continuous limit from the thermal model instead.
Datasheet no-load speed of 315 rpm at 48 V corresponds to 3150 rotor rpm, about 88% of the line-to-line RMS the bus can supply - consistent with the quoted Ke.
Dual 14-bit magnetic encoders, 1 Mbps CAN, FOC drive integrated. No-load current 0.5 Arms, rated-load speed 260 rpm at the output.
Operating ambient range -20 to 50 degC per datasheet. Class B insulation. Control board is limited to 105 degC, which can bind before the winding does in a hot enclosure.

260713 revision adds the rated-load test setup: aluminium-alloy heat sink, 90 x 85 mm, rated load measured at 100 rpm output. The earlier 251210 revision left mounting entirely unqualified. A heat sink that size is a bench fixture, not a robot joint, so the vendor rated torque still should not be read as a continuous rating in an enclosed arm.

Vendor overload endurance (ROTATING, 100 rpm, 25 degC) is now carried as structured data in overload_curves below, where the tool cross-checks the thermal model against it. It reads about 4x OPTIMISTIC against this table - see that field's note.
The 260713 revision describes a separate stall overload curve (single-phase heating 1.414x rotating) but prints no stall table for this model.
These endurance figures superseded the 251210 numbers, which differed materially (RS00 at 14 N.m: 5 s then, 3 s now). Any thermal-model fit should use the 260713 values.

overload_curves.note: 260713 manual overload endurance, rotating. Captioned 'reduced heat sink size, lower rated torque', so the heat path is worse than the 90x85 mm fixture used for the rated-torque figure - and worse than any mounting this tool models. Superseded the 251210 table, which was materially more generous (14 N.m: 5 s then, 3 s now); a vendor revising endurance DOWN is revising toward reality. Winding held to 145 degC against 180 degC insulation, per 1.3.13. NOTE: this table implies roughly 2x the copper loss that this actuator's own published T-N curve implies, and no loss term in the model reconciles the two - see est_thermal_resistances() in models.py. The disagreement is the vendor's, and it is left visible.

tn_curve.note: digitised from the 260713 manual's T-N curve image (section 1.3, 48 V), read at gridline crossings; +/-1 minor division, so roughly +/-5% in torque and +/-10 rpm. Axes are labelled in this revision, unlike 251210.
